O1.q: You are working in Unreal and you get stuck on a problem. Where should you ask for help?
choices: In the #help-desk forum on the Discord server
In a private message to a mentor
O1.explain: Ask in #help-desk on Discord. When you post, say which Unreal version you use and what you already tried, so people can help you faster.

O1.q: What do you have to do to reach the next rank?
choices: Chat a lot on the server
Stay on the server for a long time
O1.explain: Ranks come from XP, and only quests give XP. Chatting on the server does not give any.

O1.q: After you finish a quest, where is your work looked at and reviewed?
choices: Here on the site, by mentors
O1.explain: You send your work from the quest page, and mentors review it here on the site. Discord is for talking and for showing your progress.

O1.q: What are you allowed to post in the #showcase channel on Discord?
choices: Any cool art you found online
Your own work, finished or not
O1.explain: #showcase is only for work you made yourself. It does not have to be finished: work in progress is welcome.

O1.q: What do you always have to write when you send your work for a quest?
choices: How many hours you have played
O1.explain: Always write your Unreal version. Menus and features change between versions, so the right answer for you depends on which one you have.

SQ1.q: Which program do you use to download and install Unreal Engine 5?
choices: The Epic Games Launcher, in the Unreal Engine tab under Library
A zip file from the #epic-games-resources channel
SQ1.explain: Unreal Engine is installed from the Epic Games Launcher. Its Library tab is where you add, update and remove engine versions.

SQ1.q: During the install, the Options button lets you untick target platforms such as Android or iOS. Why is it a good idea to untick the ones you do not use?
choices: Because they take a lot of disk space and you do not need them yet
Because they only work on Linux
SQ1.explain: Each extra platform adds many gigabytes to the install. You can add a platform later, when you actually want to build your game for it.

SQ1.q: Can you have more than one version of Unreal Engine installed on the same computer?
choices: No, only one version at a time
Yes, they sit side by side in the Library
Only if you build the engine from source code
SQ1.explain: The Library can hold several engine versions at once. This is why you always say which version you used when you send your work.

SQ1.q: You launch the engine for the first time. Which screen opens first?
SQ1.explain: The Project Browser opens first. It is the window where you open a project you already have, or create a new one.

SQ1.q: The server rules are listed in #welcome on Discord. Which of those rules is about the engine you just installed?
choices: State your engine version when you send your work
None of the rules is about it
SQ1.explain: Rule 5 in #welcome says to state your Unreal version every time you send work. Unrealcraft teaches the current UE5 version.

SQ2.q: When you create a new project you pick a template. What does the Third Person template give you that the Blank template does not?
choices: A character you can play, a camera, input controls and a sample level
A project that only uses C++
SQ2.explain: Third Person comes with a ready-made character and a small level, so you can press Play and walk around straight away.

SQ2.q: When is the Blank template the right one to pick?
choices: When you want to build every system yourself, with nothing made for you
Only when you make a mobile game
SQ2.explain: Blank is empty on purpose. It is the right start when you do not want any ready-made character, camera or level in your way.

SQ2.q: The new-project window asks you to choose between Blueprint and C++. What does this choice decide?
choices: Whether the project starts with C++ source files
Which platform it is built for
SQ2.explain: It only decides what the project starts with. A Blueprint project can still have C++ added to it later.

SQ2.q: The new-project window has a Starter Content checkbox. What does ticking it add to your project?
SQ2.explain: Starter Content is a small set of placeholder assets. With it, your first rough rooms do not have to be plain white.

SQ2.q: Why do we ask you to keep one sandbox project and use it for all the Starter Quests?
choices: Because your work builds up, and later quests can use what you made in earlier ones
SQ2.explain: Later Starter Quests continue in the same project. The room you build in one quest is the room you light and walk through in the next ones.

SQ3.q: The viewport is the 3D window where you see your level. How do you fly around in it the way you would move a camera in a game?
choices: Hold the right mouse button and press W, A, S and D
Hold Ctrl and scroll the mouse wheel
SQ3.explain: Hold the right mouse button and use W, A, S, D to move, with Q and E to go down and up. While you fly, the mouse wheel changes your speed.

SQ3.q: You click an actor (an object in your level) to select it, then press F. What happens?
choices: The camera moves to focus on the actor
The actor is frozen in place
SQ3.explain: F stands for focus. It moves the camera so the selected actor fills the view, which is the fastest way to find something in a big level.

SQ3.q: In the viewport, what happens when you press Ctrl+1 and later press 1?
choices: Ctrl+1 saves the camera position as a bookmark, and 1 jumps back to it
SQ3.explain: These are camera bookmarks. Ctrl plus a number saves where the camera is, and pressing that number alone brings you back to the same view.

SQ3.q: PIE means Play In Editor: testing your game inside the editor. While PIE is running, what does pressing F8 do?
choices: It lets you leave your character and look around while the game keeps running
SQ3.explain: F8 ejects you from the pawn, which is the character you control. The game keeps running so you can inspect it. Press F8 again to take control back.

SQ3.q: The editor has a Play button and a Simulate button. What is the difference between them?
choices: Simulate runs the world but does not create a player for you to control
SQ3.explain: Simulate runs physics and game logic so you can watch the level work, but no player character is spawned. Play also spawns a player and gives you control of it.

SQ4.q: Asset names start with a short prefix that says what kind of asset it is. Which prefix is used for a Static Mesh?
SQ4.explain: SM_ means Static Mesh, a 3D model that does not bend. SK_ is used for a Skeletal Mesh, a model with bones that can be animated.

SQ4.q: Which prefix is used for a Material Instance?
SQ4.explain: M_ is for a parent material, and MI_ is for a Material Instance made from it.

SQ4.q: Which prefix do we put on a level (also called a map)?
SQ4.explain: Unrealcraft uses L_ for levels, for example L_FirstRoom.

SQ4.q: Why should you move or rename assets inside the Unreal editor, and never in your computer's file explorer?
choices: Because the file explorer is slower
Because the editor updates the links between assets, and the file explorer breaks them
Because only Epic is allowed to move files
SQ4.explain: Assets point to each other: a mesh points to its material, a level points to its meshes. When you move something in the Content Browser, the editor repairs those links for you. The file explorer does not know they exist.

SQ4.q: The Content Drawer is the panel that slides up to show your project's files. Which shortcut opens it?
SQ4.explain: Ctrl+Space opens the Content Drawer, and pressing it again closes it.

SQ5.q: With an actor selected in the viewport, what do the W, E and R keys switch between?
choices: The move, rotate and scale tools
SQ5.explain: W is move, E is rotate and R is scale. These tools are called transform gizmos, and the Space bar also cycles through them.

SQ5.q: You want an actor at an exact position, for example X = 200. Where do you type the number?
choices: In the Details panel, under Transform
SQ5.explain: The Details panel shows every setting of the actor you have selected. Its Transform section holds the location, rotation and scale as numbers you can type.

SQ5.q: What is the World Settings panel used for?
choices: Settings of the actor you have selected
Settings for the whole level, such as GameMode Override
The color theme of the editor
SQ5.explain: World Settings holds settings that belong to the level itself, not to one actor. Every level has its own.

SQ5.q: A blockout is a rough version of a level built from simple shapes. Why should you turn on grid snapping while you build one?
choices: Because pieces line up with no gaps and your measurements stay clean
Because you cannot save without it
SQ5.explain: With snapping on, pieces move in fixed steps, so walls meet exactly and sizes are round numbers. That makes the level easy to measure and to change later.

SQ5.q: You select an actor that is floating in the air and press the End key. What happens?
choices: The actor drops onto the surface below it
SQ5.explain: End snaps the selected actor straight down onto the floor or object under it. It is a quick way to put things on the ground.

SQ6.q: Unreal measures distance in units. By default, how long is one unit?
SQ6.explain: One unit is one centimeter, so 100 units is one meter. A door that is 200 units tall is 2 meters tall.

SQ6.q: Why should you build a room to the size of the player before you do anything else?
choices: Because a room that looks right from far away can feel wrong when you stand inside it
SQ6.explain: Size is hard to judge from the editor camera. Always check a space from the player's eye height, because that is how it will be seen in the game.

SQ6.q: What does a Player Start actor do in your level?
choices: It marks the place where the player appears when the game starts
SQ6.explain: When you press Play, the game creates the player's character at a Player Start. Without one, the player can appear in an unexpected place.

SQ6.q: You test your room and the character does not fit through the door frame. What is the right fix?
choices: Make the door wider, using the sizes you measured from the character
SQ6.explain: The character's size is the starting point, and the level is built to fit it. Measure the character, then size doors and corridors from those numbers.

SQ6.q: What does the word graybox mean in level design?
choices: The final art of a level
Plain placeholder shapes used to test the space and how the player moves through it
SQ6.explain: A graybox is the level built from simple shapes with no art. It lets you test size and flow before anyone spends time on art.

SQ7.q: Which tool lets you add the usual outdoor lights (sun, sky, fog and clouds) from one window?
SQ7.explain: The Env. Light Mixer (Environment Light Mixer) creates the Directional Light, Sky Light, atmosphere, fog and clouds, and lets you adjust them all in one place.

SQ7.q: What is Lumen in Unreal Engine 5?
choices: A plugin you have to buy
UE5's system for light that bounces off surfaces, and for reflections, worked out while the game runs
A filter added after the image is drawn
SQ7.explain: Lumen is UE5's dynamic global illumination: light bounces off surfaces and lights other things, and it updates live. You do not have to bake the lighting first.

SQ7.q: What is the goal of the lighting pass in this quest?
choices: A picture good enough for a portfolio
The player can understand the space and find the exit
SQ7.explain: The goal is a readable space: the player can see where they are and where to go. Making it pretty comes later.

SQ7.q: Which light actor do you use for the sun?
SQ7.explain: A Directional Light shines in one direction across the whole level with parallel rays, the way sunlight does.

SQ7.q: What does a Sky Light do in a scene?
choices: It draws the sun in the sky
It captures the sky and lights the scene softly from all around
SQ7.explain: A Sky Light adds soft fill light in the color of the sky. It is why areas in shadow are not completely black.

SQ8.q: A Material Instance is a copy of a material where you can change some values. Why do you edit an instance and not the parent material itself?
choices: Because changes to an instance are instant, and they do not affect other things that use the parent
Because a parent material cannot be put on a mesh
SQ8.explain: Changing a parent material makes the engine rebuild its shader, and the change shows up everywhere the material is used. An instance changes at once, and only where that instance is used.

SQ8.q: What are you able to change in a Material Instance?
choices: Only the parameters that the parent material exposes
SQ8.explain: The parent material decides which values are open to change. These open values are called parameters, and they are the only things an instance can edit.

SQ8.q: Which name prefix do you put on a Material Instance?
SQ8.explain: MI_ means Material Instance. M_ is the parent material, T_ is a texture and SM_ is a Static Mesh.

SQ8.q: Which of these does this quest NOT ask you to do?
choices: Build a master material from nothing
SQ8.explain: You only make and edit an instance here. Building a master material is a bigger job that comes later, mostly in the art specializations.

SQ8.q: How do you put a material on a mesh that is in your level?
choices: Drag it onto the mesh, or set it in the Details panel under Materials
SQ8.explain: Both ways work. Dragging is quick, and the Materials section of the Details panel lets you choose the exact material slot.

SQ9.q: In a Blueprint, which event runs when the player walks into a collision box?
SQ9.explain: On Component Begin Overlap runs at the moment something starts touching the box. The box's collision must be set to overlap for this to happen.

SQ9.q: You made a Blueprint actor named BP_Door. How do you get it into your level?
choices: Drag it from the Content Drawer into the viewport
It appears in the level by itself
SQ9.explain: A Blueprint Class is a template. Dragging it into the viewport places one copy of it in the level, and that copy is called an instance.

SQ9.q: What is the Print String node used for?
choices: The user interface of a finished game
Quick debug messages on screen and in the log
SQ9.explain: Print String writes a short message on screen. It is the fastest way to check that an event really ran.

SQ9.q: You walk into your collision box and the overlap event never runs. What should you check first?
choices: The box's Generate Overlap Events option and its collision preset
SQ9.explain: Most overlap problems are collision settings. The box needs Generate Overlap Events turned on, and a collision preset that overlaps the player.

choices: Once, when the actor starts playing
It never runs in Play In Editor
SQ9.explain: BeginPlay runs one time when the actor enters the game, so it is the place for setup. Event Tick is the one that runs every frame.

SQ10.q: A pawn is the thing the player controls. Where do you set which pawn appears when the level starts?
choices: In the GameMode's Default Pawn Class, or through GameMode Override in World Settings
SQ10.explain: The GameMode holds the rules of the game, including which pawn the player gets. World Settings can choose a different GameMode for one level.

SQ10.q: Why is it useful to keep a mannequin that does not move standing in your level while you build?
choices: It is a size reference you can always see while you build
SQ10.explain: With a human-sized figure in view, you can judge the size of doors and rooms without pressing Play every time.

SQ10.q: Unreal has a Pawn class and a Character class. What is the difference?
choices: A Character is a Pawn that already has a capsule, a mesh and walking movement
A Character cannot be controlled by a player
SQ10.explain: Character is a ready-made kind of Pawn. It gives you walking, jumping and falling without building them yourself.

SQ10.q: You press Play and you are a camera floating in the air, not your character. What is the most likely cause?
choices: The GameMode's default pawn is not your character
SQ10.explain: The game spawned its default pawn, not yours. Check GameMode Override in World Settings, and the Default Pawn Class of that GameMode.

SQ10.q: What do you have to do for this quest to count as done?
choices: Walk through your space and fix one thing that felt wrong
SQ10.explain: Test, notice a problem, fix it. This loop is how every level gets better, and this quest is your first time through it.

SQ11.q: Do you have to install Visual Studio to finish this quest?
choices: No, this quest is only reading
Only if you are a programmer
SQ11.explain: This quest only asks you to read and understand. Visual Studio, the program used to write C++, is installed later in the Programming path.

SQ11.q: Which of these is a normal reason to write something in C++ and not in Blueprint?
choices: It needs a lot of performance, or it is a core system that many Blueprints build on
SQ11.explain: Heavy work and core systems go in C++. Content, and values you want to adjust quickly, stay in Blueprint.

SQ11.q: Can a Blueprint be built on top of a class that was written in C++?
choices: Yes. A common setup is a C++ base class with Blueprint children
SQ11.explain: Yes, and it is very common: programmers write the base in C++, and designers make Blueprint versions of it. It is also the Rank 3 capstone of the Programming path.

SQ11.q: Why do designers like to work in Blueprint?
choices: They can try changes quickly and see the logic as a graph, without compiling C++
It runs faster in the game
SQ11.explain: In Blueprint you change something and test it right away. That speed of trying things is the reason Blueprint exists.

SQ11.q: You chose Level Design as your specialization. After this quest, how much C++ do you still have to do?
choices: Rewrite your work in C++ at Rank 4
One small taster (a C++ hello or a GAS video), and nothing is locked behind it
SQ11.explain: Level designers only do one short taster from the other side. They never have to rewrite their work in C++.
